stories.headline: Severe heatwave grips South and Southeast Asia, setting power-demand records

key_facts.fact: Northern Vietnam's peak power demand hit a record 24,722 MW on the afternoon of May 24, up 16% from the previous Sunday, forcing grid operator NSMO to start up expensive oil-fired plants (O Mon I units S1 and S2) to meet peak demand for May 25.
National Vietnamese electricity consumption on May 23 reached 1.116 billion kWh - the highest ever recorded on a Sunday, 12.8% above the prior Sunday - with the system peaking at 53,512 MW.

In India's Odisha state, peak power demand surged to a record 6,739 MW amid temperatures near 45C, almost 300 MW above last year's maximum, with Tata Power-led distribution companies on full emergency footing.

In Telangana, at least 16 people died of heatstroke across seven districts over the weekend, prompting the state to announce 4 lakh rupees ex-gratia for each victim's family; Khammam recorded 45.4C on May 23.
The India Meteorological Department issued a fresh heatwave warning for nine Telangana districts for May 25 and warned that severe-heatwave conditions would continue through May 26.

stories.headline: Crypto analytics firm Elliptic raises $120M Series D at $670M valuation

key_facts.fact: Elliptic, a digital-asset analytics company, closed a $120 million Series D led by One Peak, with participation from Nasdaq Ventures, Deutsche Bank and the British Business Bank; the round values Elliptic at $670 million.
Existing backers AlbionVC, Evolution Equity Partners and J.P. Morgan also support the company; CEO Simone Maini said 'financial systems are being rebuilt on-chain.'

stories.headline: HSBC lifts 2026 oil forecast to $95, warns energy shock is forcing rate hikes

key_facts.fact: HSBC raised its 2026 Brent crude average forecast by $15 to $95 a barrel, warning the supply shock's impact on global inflation is now hard to reverse even if a US-Iran deal reopens the Strait of Hormuz.
HSBC expects the European Central Bank to hike rates 25 basis points each in June, July and September, with the Bank of England and Bank of Japan likely to hike between June and July.
From February to April, energy contributed more than one percentage point to CPI in major US and eurozone economies, and as much as 3.9 points in Thailand and 2.8 points in the Philippines.

US trailing inflation has hit roughly a three-year high near 3.8%, with the Cleveland Fed nowcast pointing to about 4.18% for May, after Iran's late-February closure of the Strait of Hormuz halted some 20 million barrels a day of petroleum (about 20% of global demand).

US April CPI rose to 3.8% year-on-year and PPI jumped to 6%, while the 30-year Treasury yield broke above 5% for the first time since 2007; markets see the Fed possibly dropping its easing bias at its June meeting under new Chair Kevin Warsh.

stories.headline: Huawei unveils 'Tau Scaling Law' to chase 1.4nm-equivalent chips by 2031 without EUV

key_facts.fact: He Tingbo, president of Huawei's semiconductor business and director of its Scientist Committee, presented the Tau (τ) Scaling Law in a keynote titled 'New Semiconductor Path in Practice' at the 2026 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS) in Shanghai.

The Tau Scaling Law proposes replacing geometric scaling (shrinking transistors) with 'time scaling' — using τ to denote signal propagation delay — claiming chips that run faster and more efficiently even without the world's most advanced fabrication equipment restricted by US sanctions.

By 2031, Huawei expects the high-end chips it designs using the τ Scaling Law to feature transistor density equivalent to 14 Å (1.4nm) processes — near the projected global frontier that TSMC and Samsung are expected to reach via conventional lithography.

Kirin chips scheduled to launch in Fall 2026 will be the first to adopt Huawei's LogicFolding architecture, which shortens critical-path wiring to reduce signal delay; Huawei says it has designed and mass-produced 381 chips based on the τ Scaling Law over the past six years.
Chinese semiconductor stocks rallied on the announcement: SMIC jumped more than 17% in Shanghai trading, Cambricon climbed nearly 10%, and Piotech gained over 18%.

Huawei released no independent benchmark or manufacturing data; analysts caution that an 'equivalent' 1.4nm density does not match a true 1.4nm-class process from a leading foundry, and Huawei's current Kirin chips are made by SMIC at processes estimated at roughly 7nm.

stories.headline: Ex-Citadel quants' fintech Moment raises $78M led by Index Ventures

key_facts.fact: Moment, a fintech founded by former Citadel Securities quantitative traders and researchers, raised $78 million in a round led by Index Ventures, with participation from existing investors Andreessen Horowitz and Avra.
The company, which builds AI agent infrastructure for wealth management and counts Edward Jones and LPL as clients, last raised $36 million in July 2025.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical 'Magnifica humanitas' urges a slower pace on AI

key_facts.fact: Pope Leo XIV released his first encyclical, 'Magnifica humanitas: On Safeguarding the Human Person in the Time of Artificial Intelligence,' on Monday, May 25, 2026; the text was signed May 15, the 135th anniversary of Leo XIII's labor encyclical Rerum novarum.

The encyclical calls for 'prudence, rigorous evaluation and even, at times, a slower pace in adopting AI,' and for 'more active political involvement that is capable of slowing things down when everything is accelerating.'
In the ~43,000-word document, Pope Leo urged governments to slow the development of AI systems and decried 'new forms of slavery' in AI and tech supply chains.

The encyclical argues AI cannot be considered morally neutral, calls for adequate AI policies, legal frameworks, independent oversight and user education, and says data 'should not be treated as something to be sold off or entrusted to a select few' but managed as a 'common or shared good.'

The encyclical warns AI 'can imitate and simulate the person, but it does not possess a moral conscience, empathy, or affective, relational or spiritual capabilities,' and cautions against the 'technocratic paradigm' where choices are dictated by efficiency and profit.

Christopher Olah, co-founder of Anthropic and head of its AI interpretability research, was among the official speakers who presented the encyclical with the Pope at the Vatican's Synod Hall on May 25.
A section of the encyclical describing AI's unpredictability suggests influence from Anthropic, whose co-founder attended the unveiling.
The encyclical also calls for AI regulation and for protection of children against hypersexualized AI-generated images.

stories.headline: Russia hits Kyiv region with Oreshnik missile in massive attack; EU vows more pressure

key_facts.fact: Russia launched a massive combined missile-and-drone attack on Ukraine overnight into May 24, firing 90 missiles and 600 drones; Ukraine's Air Force said it shot down or suppressed 604 targets (55 missiles and 549 drones), with Kyiv the main target.

President Zelensky said Russia used its nuclear-capable Oreshnik intermediate-range ballistic missile for the third time in the war, striking Bila Tserkva in Kyiv Oblast - the first time the weapon has been directed at the Kyiv region.
At least two people were killed and 83 wounded in the bombardment, one of the heaviest on Kyiv since the war began.

Russia's Defense Ministry confirmed using the Oreshnik and other missile types to strike Ukrainian military command-and-control facilities, air bases and military-industrial sites, calling it retaliation for Ukrainian strikes on civilian facilities in Russia.
At a UN Security Council emergency meeting requested by Russia, Ukraine's ambassador Andrii Melnyk dismissed Russia's war-crimes accusations as a 'pure propaganda show.'

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas called the Oreshnik use 'reckless nuclear brinkmanship' and said EU foreign ministers will meet next week to dial up pressure on Russia, while Macron, Merz and von der Leyen condemned the strikes.

stories.headline: US and Iran near deal to end war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Regional officials said the US is close to a deal with Iran that would end the war, reopen the Strait of Hormuz and see Iran give up its stockpile of highly enriched uranium.

Trump said the agreement, a 'Memorandum of Understanding pertaining to PEACE,' had been 'largely negotiated' after calls with Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan, Bahrain and, separately, Israel.

A senior US official said Sunday the deal is expected to be signed 'in the coming days,' with wording still being finalized, after the broad framework was approved by Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei.

Under the emerging agreement the Strait of Hormuz would gradually reopen in parallel with the US ending its blockade, the US would allow Iran to sell oil through sanctions waivers, and a 60-day period would cover negotiations on Iran's nuclear program; the draft also includes ending the Israel-Hezbollah fighting in Lebanon.

Netanyahu said he and Trump agreed any final agreement 'must eliminate the nuclear danger' - meaning dismantling Iran's enrichment sites and removing enriched material - while the NYT reported the US has largely excluded Israel from the talks.

stories.headline: Peking University spinout Vifan raises hundreds of millions of yuan for a domestic robot 'brain' chip

key_facts.fact: Beijing Vifan Intelligence Technology, incubated from Peking University's brain-inspired chip lab (PAICORE Lab) and founded in May 2025, has completed a seed round of several hundred million yuan to build a fully domestic 'brain' computing chip for embodied-AI robots.

The round was co-led by Zhongguancun Capital and its Qihang Investment arm, with participation from the Shanghai Future Industry Fund, Shixi Capital, Biwin Storage, Yanchuang Group, Haiyi Investment, and Tanyuan Venture.

Vifan has developed a Brain-Inspired GPU (BiGPU) architecture that fuses neuromorphic spiking-neural-network computing with general-purpose GPU compute, aiming to cut power use while keeping broad algorithm compatibility for robot perception, AI inference, and motion control.

The company is positioning itself as a domestic alternative to Nvidia's Jetson series, which dominates the robot-brain chip market but is described as costly with limited local support; Vifan targets chip production in the second quarter of 2027.

Co-founder Yin Jilei is a Peking University graduate with more than 20 years in semiconductors, previously COO and VP of R&D at Witmem Technology and a chip R&D director at IBM and GlobalFoundries; core team members come from IBM, Huawei, and Tencent.
